candidates.statement: LinkedIn exists to let professionals connect and live in the business world.
candidates.modality: descriptive belief about the platform's role
context: Answer to 'what is Linkedin to you'

evidence_candidates.quote: It exists out there just to allow kind of professionals to connect and you know, live in the business world.

candidates.statement: Network on LinkedIn by connecting with other colleagues and past classmates to see what they are up to.
candidates.modality: habitual; one of several recurring uses
context: Listed first among the things he does on LinkedIn

evidence_candidates.quote: So some of the things that I do on Linkedin are going to be networking just connecting with other colleagues, or maybe kind of past classmates see what they're up to.

candidates.statement: Do a lot of marketing on LinkedIn because the exposure is far better than what Google Ads, Facebook or other channels deliver.
candidates.modality: explicit, recurring ('we focus a lot on marketing')
context: Marketing is central in his field
They work with a lot of other professionals

evidence_candidates.quote: In some areas, you know, marketing the exposure, there is far better than we might get, you know, through Google ads or Facebook out of other channels. So we focus a lot on marketing.

candidates.statement: Recruit through LinkedIn as a good source of many people at a fairly low cost compared with competitors.
candidates.modality: explicit, recurring ('we do a lot of recruiting')
context: Compared with some of the other competitors

evidence_candidates.quote: We do a lot of recruiting as well through Linkedin. just good source a lot of people. And it's fairly low cost compared to some of the other competitors.

candidates.statement: Look at other job openings and salary ranges on LinkedIn for himself, keeping an eye and ear to the ground to stay motivated.
candidates.modality: soft and occasional ('sometimes it's nice to kind of poke around')
context: Personal use rather than company use

evidence_candidates.quote: And then even looking for jobs for myself. Yeah, sometimes it's nice to kind of poke around. See what else is out there in the world, and just see what some of the salary ranges and things like that, you know, always keeps you motivated.

candidates.statement: Check LinkedIn for community events when he has the availability and bandwidth, because email alone gives him no chance to keep up with everything.
candidates.modality: conditional preference ('it's nice that when I have the availability')
context: Only when availability and bandwidth allow
Email is a fire hose he cannot keep up with

evidence_candidates.quote: I drink from the fire hose of emails and there's no chance that I would be able to otherwise keep up with everything. So it's nice that when I have the availability, and I think I, you know, can have the bandwidth. I can go on and check and see kind of what events are, you know, being put on the community.

candidates.statement: Signal to clients that he exists and has credentials and degrees, so his profile lends a bit of credibility.
candidates.modality: explicit ('it's mostly to just signal')
context: Stated as the main role LinkedIn plays for him

evidence_candidates.quote: It's mostly to just signal to like my other to my clients, for example, that I I. You know I exist. I'm a person who, you know, has credentials, and I have, you know, degrees, and it just lends a little bit of a you know. a bit of credibility.

candidates.statement: Give people a way to check that he is who he says he is, not a scammer, with a picture matching how he appears on Zoom or in person.
candidates.modality: explicit ('another resource for people to check in')
context: Tied to emails he sends to clients

evidence_candidates.quote: It's more of just a you know, another resource for people to check in and just make sure. Okay, I'm not like a Scammer. I'm not a, you know. If they get an email from me I am who I say I am, and the picture there matches the picture that they see on, you know, Zoom, or or you know, when I meet in person.

candidates.statement: LinkedIn has not played much of a role in his own professional development.
candidates.modality: explicit denial ('I can't say it's actually played that much of a role')
context: Career opportunities came through word of mouth and existing networks

evidence_candidates.quote: So for my own professional development. I can't say it's actually played that much of a role.

candidates.statement: Treat cost as a consideration for LinkedIn marketing resources, because they charge an arm and a leg.
candidates.modality: explicit consideration ('cost is definitely a consideration')
context: Said while praising the marketing resources

evidence_candidates.quote: I think a lot of the marketing resources are are pretty good. I mean, they do charge you an arm and a leg. So I think cost is definitely a consideration there.

candidates.statement: The tools LinkedIn offers for posting marketing content are very easy and user friendly.
candidates.modality: positive evaluation of an existing capability
context: Described as making LinkedIn a good tool for broad based marketing

evidence_candidates.quote: some of the tools that they have to like post you know, marketing things are are very, very easy and user friendly.

candidates.statement: Pay to have a post recommended more, with cost and expected boost stated up front, so he can keep track of impressions and marketing metrics.
candidates.modality: capability described appreciatively ('that process is just really simple')
context: Recommendations and paid boosting are part of the marketing workflow

evidence_candidates.quote: They have like recommendations. You can pay to have it be recommended a little bit more. And that process is just really simple. They just tell you here's how much it's gonna cost. And you know, here's how much it's gonna get boosted. So you can kind of keep track of all your impressions and all of your different marketing metrics.

candidates.statement: Use LinkedIn's e-learning content (Lynda) for a quick deep dive into a technology stack or to do marketing better, because its quality exceeds YouTube and other sources.
candidates.modality: past preference ('I did like when they purchased Linda')
context: Compared with YouTube and other free resources

evidence_candidates.quote: I did like when they purchased Linda, which was their kind of e-learning platform. You know, there is some kind of helpful stuff. If you want to do kind of a quick, deep dive into a certain. You know technology stack, or you want to kind of get a better understanding of like, how do I, you know, do something in marketing a little bit better. that was actually one of the better places to go, because in terms of quality it would definitely exceed. You know what you might find on Youtube or some of those other resources.

candidates.statement: Post a marketing post for awareness, for example about something interesting happening while at a conference.
candidates.modality: typical task ('the task would probably be kind of posting')
context: Walked through as his typical professional task

evidence_candidates.quote: So I think the task would probably be kind of posting, marketing information are posting like a marketing post just for awareness.
So let's say, I'm at a conference. And yeah, something interesting is happening. Typically what we'll do is yeah, post something about it.

candidates.statement: Toggle between the company's LinkedIn page and his personal profile, or both, when publishing a post.
candidates.modality: capability he uses in the posting flow
context: He operates both the company page and his own profile

evidence_candidates.quote: Which says, just start a post. and from there I can choose because I operate the Linkedin for my company, as well as for kind of my special profile. I can toggle between one or both, so if I'm posting as myself. I would choose myself.

candidates.statement: Schedule the post for 9 AM the next morning instead of the evening, so it reaches people when they first show up at the office and gets more impressions.
candidates.modality: explicit decision ('I'm going to be posted at 9 Am. Tomorrow')
context: Evening posts get fewer impressions

evidence_candidates.quote: most people are going to be logging in, probably tomorrow morning. And so it doesn't really make sense, you know, in the evening, to post it. It's just not going to get as many impressions. So I'm going to be posted at, you know. 9 Am. Tomorrow, when people 1st show up at the office, and I'll get a nice kind of boost in some of the impressions.

candidates.statement: Embed images, videos, nice backgrounds and emojis in the post to give it more polish.
candidates.modality: available tools he uses while writing the post
context: Part of composing the post

evidence_candidates.quote: I can write my post. and they have, you know, a couple of little tools where I can embed, you know. images, videos, or, you know. kind of create a little more pop and circumstance, like nice backgrounds and emojis.

candidates.statement: Once posted, the post goes to the feed, starts getting interactions and hopefully eventually wins some business.
candidates.modality: hopeful expectation ('hopefully, eventually')
context: Described as the downstream effect of posting

evidence_candidates.quote: So once I've posted it, it goes out to the network and it's on the feed, so I'll start to kind of get some interactions. And you know. hopefully, eventually win some business.

candidates.statement: Avoid cold calls or cold adds on LinkedIn and typically only reach out to people he already knows.
candidates.modality: soft habit ('I don't often', 'I don't reach out too much')
context: Distinguishes warm contacts from strangers

evidence_candidates.quote: So I don't often kind of reach out and connect with you know other folks. It's like more. If it's somebody I know, I'll reach out and add them but I don't reach out too much as kind of cold call or cold. Add

candidates.statement: Search for a specific prospect, pull up the profile, look for common threads in the background, and then maybe add them.
candidates.modality: hedged habit ('maybe I'll search', 'maybe I'll add them')
context: Prospect example: a C-suite executive at a company they want to sell to

evidence_candidates.quote: maybe I'll search for their name if there's somebody that I'm you know, interested in learning more about. Maybe they're a C, you know, c-suite at a company that we're looking to sell to. I want to get a little background on them, I'll you know, search them in the search function, pull up their profile, kind of take a quick look at their background to see if there's any kind of common threads, and then maybe I'll you know I'll add them.

candidates.statement: He uses LinkedIn about 4 out of 5 days a week, checking it at least once on most days.
candidates.modality: reported usage frequency
context: Answer to how often he uses LinkedIn

evidence_candidates.quote: I'd say, let's let's call it 4 out of 5 days a week I'm on Linkedin in some way, shape or form.

candidates.statement: Post recruiting ads in the Laravel community job board (Lara jobs) because it yields better candidates than posting on LinkedIn.
candidates.modality: conditional generalization ('if you post something there')
context: Laravel community is small
Applies to recruiting

evidence_candidates.quote: for example, recruiting like the Laravel community is pretty small. And you know, Lara jobs. If you post something there, you actually get better candidates than you might get from yeah posting something on Linkedin. So in terms of recruiting. Some tools are just better

candidates.statement: LinkedIn is the only game in town and has carved out a niche for professional development.
candidates.modality: belief about the market ('I think')
context: Contrast with specialized recruiting boards

evidence_candidates.quote: but in terms of like professional development. I think Linkedin is rare in that. It's kind of the only game in town.

candidates.statement: The amount of ads and targeted content feels like too much, clouds the feed and puts a lot of irrelevant stuff there; this is his biggest frustration.
candidates.modality: frustration ('would probably be the biggest frustration')
context: Answer to the obstacles and frustrations question

evidence_candidates.quote: So I think one frustration would be, you know, sometimes the amount of ads and the amount of you know targeted stuff feels a little much. It just kind of clouds your feed, and there's a lot of irrelevant stuff there.

candidates.statement: Certain parts of the interface are too cluttered, throwing in information to make it busy; when he is on a mission the rest is just added noise he does not care for.
candidates.modality: frustration ('don't necessarily care for it')
context: Mission example: posting something to turn into impressions

evidence_candidates.quote: And then certain parts of the interface. our just too cluttered. I think they throw a lot of information just to make it very busy. They want you click it everywhere. But in certain cases, yeah, I'm there for a reason. I have a mission. I gotta post something. I want to turn that into, you know impressions, and having that, all of this other stuff is kind of just added noise. And I yeah, don't necessarily care for it.

candidates.statement: LinkedIn has focused more on marketing tools, becoming more targeted so that posts get in front of the right people.
candidates.modality: observation of platform evolution ('it's tried to focus on')
context: Answer to how LinkedIn has evolved

evidence_candidates.quote: I think what it's tried to focus on a lot more is, you know, marketing tools so becoming a lot more targeted so that your posts make in front of the right people.

candidates.statement: There are new AI tools on LinkedIn to help develop content for posts, which he finds new and interesting.
candidates.modality: observation plus interest ('pretty new and interesting')
context: Mentioned in the evolution answer

evidence_candidates.quote: They built, you know, there's some new like AI tools to help with developing content for posts. Yeah, that's pretty new and interesting.

candidates.statement: Get more automated support for content development, so the company does not have to have as big a marketing team.
candidates.modality: wish ('would be great to have more of that automated')
context: Named as the biggest thing he would add

evidence_candidates.quote: Probably the biggest would just be, you know, support for content development, and then, you know, would be great to have more of that kind of automated. So we don't have to have as big of a marketing team, or that's always a pain, because.

candidates.statement: Be able to post professional looking stuff without having it reviewed six times and going through the whole marketing funnel, since design is at a premium and takes a while.
candidates.modality: wish ('it'd be great to be able to post')
context: Design is at a premium
Review rounds take time

evidence_candidates.quote: Design is at a premium, and that just always takes a while. So it'd be great to be able to post, you know, professional looking stuff without having to be, you know, reviewed 6 times, and go through kind of the whole marketing funnel.
